comment: Known legitimate divergences between the Rust port (calibrated to dss_capi
0.14.5) and ORIGINAL EPRI OpenDSS engines, consumed by the opt-in EPRI
channel only: corpus_live_opendss partitions its report into known/new and
DSS_LIVE_OPENDSS_ASSERT=1 fails only on NEW divergences; ab_compare.py
--known-diffs reclassifies fully-matching cases as known_diverged.
This is a triage inventory, NOT a mute button: every entry carries a
non-empty `cause`, entries are matched by substring on (case label, panic
reason), first match wins, and per-entry hit counts are reported so dead
entries surface and get pruned as upstream deltas are ported.
NEVER consulted by the mandatory gate or its tolerances.
Entry kinds (`kind`, default 'diff'): 'diff' = the case runs on the listed
revs but legitimately diverges (matched on the failure reason); 'skip' =
the case is not expected to run/converge on the listed revs at all — the
EPRI channel skips the comparison up front (matched on `case_contains`
only; `reason_contains` unused) and reports it under `known_skipped`.
Optional `ab_contains` overrides `reason_contains` when matching
ab_compare.py issue strings (different wording than the Rust panics);
entries without it and without a matching Rust-shaped phrase simply never
reclassify there. Modeled on DSS-Python tests/compare_outputs.py
KNOWN_COM_DIFF (BSD-3), translated to our first-failure-reason match shape.

entries.cause: Solve/control iteration-count deltas: Delphi-vs-FPC last-ulp rounding shifts convergence-check outcomes, and dss_capi's reworked controls iterate differently (AutoTrans+RegControl reg-tap 6-vs-3; GenDispatcher dispatch 20-vs-4 / 31-vs-5 on r4088). The port matches the pinned FPC oracle's EXACT count (mandatory gate green); EPRI's Delphi settles a near-identical state (V ~3.5e-4) in a different number of control iterations. Identical magnitude vs r4133 (solver + these controls behaviorally identical r4088=r4133 — RegControl/GenDispatcher byte-identical; Solution.pas differs only in inert progress-form plumbing + a commented-out debug WriteLn, AutoTrans.pas only in two read-only PropertyHelp strings).

entries.cause: EPRI pads monitor header channel names with a leading space (' VAngle1'); dss_capi strips them. Narrowed to r3723 by WP-U2.6: zero hits on the r4088 AND r4133 sweeps because the harness `compare_monitor` now normalizes the Delphi monitor-CSV header artifact directly (leading-space + trailing-empty columns; WP-U2.1 combo-restore audit fix) — so the header no longer surfaces as a compare divergence on the EPRI channel. Retained on r3723 (its original triage provenance, not re-swept this WP). NOTE: the `compare_monitor` header normalization (harness/mod.rs trim + trailing-empty drop) is rev-INDEPENDENT — it applies to the expected side for every EPRI rev, r3723 included — so this entry is most likely already dead on r3723 too; a future r3723 re-sweep (its only residual cost is a zero-hit prune warning) will confirm and prune it.
entries.source: triage 2026-07 r3723 (8 controls cases); cf. DSS-Python compare_outputs.py string handling; narrowed WP-U2.6 (0 hits r4088+r4133 post harness header-normalization)

entries.cause: Sequence-magnitude monitor channel (V2, mode=32 seq-voltage) drifts ~2.4e-6 abs / rel ~1.1e-5 (0.21350601 vs 0.21350846) — above the 1e-6 monitor-channel abs floor. The symmetrical-component transform (Fortescue A-matrix over complex node voltages) amplifies Delphi-vs-FPC transcendental last-ulp; the port matches the pinned FPC 0.14.5 oracle (mandatory gate green). Meters/Monitor.pas is byte-identical r4088=r4133, so the drift is identical against both EPRI revs — an FPC<->Delphi Seq floor, not an r4088->r4133 change (dss_capi's own dsspy_validation loosens Seq* categories to 1e-2 for the same reason).

entries.cause: The documented r4088->r4133 harmonics-mode voltage move on the IEEE_519 filter deck (WP-U0.2 surprise, docs/upgrade/sweeps/r4088_vs_r4133.md): node V ~4.3e-4 at pcc (rel ~4e-4) with the assembled Y bit-identical (Yf=0). WP-U2.6 SOURCE-CONFIRMED there is nothing to port: SolutionAlgs.pas (harmonics driver), PCElements/Load.pas, General/Spectrum.pas and Common/YMatrix.pas are all byte-identical r4088=r4133 (Solution.pas differs only in progress-form plumbing + commented-out debug WriteLn), so no harmonics/injection algorithm changed. The move is determinism-proven per engine (r4088<->r4088 and r4133<->r4133 both match) => a build-to-build Delphi last-ulp drift amplified by the near-resonance of the 519 filter (an ill-conditioned harmonics fixpoint), NOT a portable behavior change. The port matches the pinned FPC 0.14.5 oracle (mandatory gate green) and its own physically-correct harmonics solution; documented upstream, no port action. SCOPE NOTE: the case_contains='IEEE_519' + reason_contains=['entry ',' differs'] match is deliberately broad (mirroring the sibling harmonics-yfingerprint-drift / autotrans-regcontrol-tap floor entries) — it absorbs ANY node-voltage 'entry N differs' on the three IEEE_519 decks on r4133, not only the specific ~4.3e-4 pcc-node move. A materially different IEEE_519 divergence (different node/magnitude) would therefore be classified 'known' here rather than surfacing as NEW under ASSERT; if the source ever ceases to be byte-identical r4088=r4133 on the harmonics path, re-triage this class instead of assuming it.
entries.source: WP-U0.2 r4088<->r4133 sweep + WP-U2.6 r4133 sweep (HarmonicsTMode/HarmonicsVariableLoad/Matlab HarmonicT_MATLAB IEEE_519.DSS)

The port matches the pinned FPC oracle (mandatory gate green); the committed capi015<->r4088 sweep shows the same 'regcontrols differ: [rat]' engine-to-engine, so it is FPC-vs-Delphi, not a port bug. entries.cause: Circuit-reduction produces a different reduced network FPC(port) vs EPRI(Delphi): reduce keep/merge/switch handling collapses branches differently, so a reduced Line YPrim can differ structurally (e.g. a merged branch vs a retained pseudo-switch Y=500) and node V drifts. The port matches the pinned FPC oracle's reduced network EXACTLY (mandatory gate green, incl. YPrim); capi015<->r4088 confirms reduce_mergeparallel drifts engine-to-engine. Reduction is not a Rung-1 item (not in WP-U1.*).
